title: Preparation of scFv Stabilized Chromatosomes for Single-Particle Cryo-EM
author: Zhou, Bai
materials: CRITICAL: A plasmid with an array of repeat sequences tends to be unstable when propagated in bacterial strains, therefore it is critical to utilize a stable cell line such as NEB Stable cells or Invitrogen One Shot stbl2 cells. After transformation, check the plasmid isolated from several colonies by restriction enzyme digestion or DNA sequencing. This analysis is equally critical for the production of the desired DNA with high yield.1.Transform 1 μL of pUC19-197x16_W601 plasmid (∼100 ng/μL) into 50 μL NEB Stable cells following the manufacturer’s protocol and spread around ∼20 μL cells onto an LB agar plate containing 100 ug/mL ampicillin. Incubate the plate in a 37°C incubator for ∼18 h.2.Label 4 colonies separately, then inoculate each colony into 10 mL of LB medium containing 100 ug/mL ampicillin in a 50 mL Falcon tube. Grow in a 37°C incubator shaker at 220 rpm for 6 - 8 h.3.Transfer 4 mL of cell culture from each tube to four new Falcon tubes. Extract plasmids using the Promega Mini-Prep Kit, following the manufacturer’s protocol.4.Digest 200 ng of each purified plasmid using PstI and EcoRI restriction enzymes, which should yield a 3.2 kb insert (16 × 197 bp) band and a 2.7 kb pUC vector band when resolved in a 2% agarose gel (Figure 2, left, lanes 1–4). Plasmid digested with SmaI restriction enzyme alone should produce a 197 bp W601 DNA band and 2.9 kb vector band (Figure 2, right, lanes 1–4).Figure 2Verification the plasmids after transformation(A) A diagram of the plasmid map and restriction enzyme sites. Map is created by SnapGene.(B) Purified plasmids digested with restriction enzymes and run on a 2% agarose gel.5.Once the plasmids are verified, the corresponding cell cultures can be combined and equally distributed to six flasks containing 1 L 2x YT cell culture medium. Incubate the cell cultures in a 37°C incubator shaker set at 250 rpm for ∼18–24 h.6.Harvest the cells by centrifugation at 4000xg, 4°C for 30 min in an Eppendorf 5810R centrifuge. Perform large scale plasmid preparation by following the published protocol (Dyer et al., 2004).7.The typical yield of plasmid from 6 L of cell culture is ∼80 - 120 mg. To release the 16 copies of 197 bp W601 DNA, digest the plasmid with 10 U SmaI restriction enzyme per mg plasmid in 1x NEB Cutsmart buffer, adjust the plasmid concentration to ∼2 mg/mL with deionized (DI) water, and incubate in a 37°C incubator for 18 h.8.Analyze the SmaI plasmid digestion on a 2% agarose gel. The presence of multiple bands other than the 197 bp DNA and 2.9 kb plasmid DNA suggests that the digestion is incomplete. In this case, add 50% more enzyme and incubate another 18 h.9.Once the digestion is complete, Aliquot to ∼20 mL in several 50 mL Falcon tubes. Precipitate the plasmid backbone (2.9 kb band) by stepwise adding 40% PEG 6000 to the digestion solution ranging from 4% to 6%, while simultaneously adding 4 M NaCl to a final concentration of 0.5 M. Mix well. When the mixture turns cloudy, place the tubes on ice for at least 1 h to further precipitate the plasmid backbone DNA.10.Pellet the plasmid backbone DNA by centrifugation at 4000xg, 4°C for 30 min in an Eppendorf 5810R centrifuge. Decant ∼15 mL of supernatant to each 50 mL Falcon tube and precipitate the 197 bp DNA by adding ∼30 mL of cold ethanol.11.Pellet the 197 bp DNA by centrifugation at 4000xg, 4°C for 30 min in an Eppendorf 5810R centrifuge, discard the supernatant, wash the pellet with 70% ethanol three times, air dry the pellet and then redissolve it in TE 10/1 (10 mM Tris, 1 mM EDTA, pH8.0) buffer.12.Extract the DNA once with phenol:chloroform:isoamyl alchohol (25:24:1) (PCIA) and then with chloroform:isoamyl alcohol (CIA) to remove residual enzyme and PEG 6000. Precipitate the DNA using ethanol, and then redissolve it in TE 10/1 buffer. The typical yield of 197 bp DNA is ∼30 - 40 mg. Store the 197 bp DNA at 4oC at a concentration of ∼ 5 mg/mL.Alternatives: DNA can also be prepared using a large-scale PCR method as detailed in a recent protocol (Nodelman et al., 2020).

Folded scFv is stabilized by four disulfide bonds. Recombinant scFv often forms inclusion bodies in E. coli cells due to the reducing environment in the bacterial cytoplasm. We have tested scFv expression in NEB SHuffle T7 Competent E. coli cells that provide an oxidative environment, however scFv expression still results in inclusion body formation. Here we describe the refolding and purification of scFv from the inclusion body (Figure 3), with modifications of the previous protocol (Pastan and Ho, 2010) .Figure 3Diagram of the workflow for refolding and purification of scFv from the inclusion body

1.Transform 1 μl pETHis6TEV-scFv plasmid into 20 μl BL21(DE3) RIPL cells following the manufacturer’s protocol. Spread ∼20 μL transformed cells onto an LB agar plate containing 100 μg/mL ampicillin. Incubate the plate at 37°C for 18 h.2.Inoculate a single colony into 10 mL LB medium containing 100 μg/mL ampicillin and grow in a 37°C incubator shaker at 220 rpm for 14 h.3.Dilute the 10 mL LB cell culture into 1 L of 2x YT medium containing 100 μg/mL ampicillin. Continue to grow until the OD600 of the cell culture reaches 0.8.4.Cool the cell culture and the incubator shaker to 25°C. Induce protein expression by adding 0.5 mM IPTG and continue to grow the cells in the 25°C incubator shaker at 220 rpm for 16 h.5.Harvest the cells by centrifugation at 3000xg, 10 min at 4°C in a Beckman Coulter Avanti J-20I centrifuge. Resuspend the cells in 35 mL Lysis buffer (50 mM Tris-HCl, pH7.5, 100 mM NaCl, 1 mM EDTA). Add 0.5 mL 50 mg/mL lysozyme stock solution and freeze the cells on dry ice.6.Thaw the cells in a 42°C water bath. The cell lysate should be very sticky. Break up the sticky cell lysate using a Misonix sonicator for 4 min (15 s ON, 1 min OFF with 15% power level), keeping the sample on ice.7.Pellet the inclusion body by centrifugation at 27,000xg for 20 min at 4°C in a Beckman Coulter Avanti J-20I centrifuge.8.Discard the supernatant, resuspend the pellet in wash buffer (50 mM Tris-HCl, pH7.5, 100 mM NaCl, 1 mM EDTA, 1% Triton X-100). If the pellet is still sticky, break it up with sonication for 30 s. Collect the inclusion body pellets by centrifugation. Decant the supernatant.9.Wash the pellet two more time using lysis buffer and collect the inclusion body pellets as above.Pause point: The scFv inclusion body pellet can be stored at −80°C up to a month at this step.Optional: Inclusion bodies can be prepared from the bacterial cells using a commercially available reagent such as B-per Bacterial Protein Extraction Reagent (Pierce; Thermo Scientific Life Science, Rockford, IL, USA). Add 2.5 mL (official document states 4 mL) of the reagent containing 500 ug of lysozyme (10 μL of 50 mg/mL stock) and 20 U of DNase I (8 μL of 2500 U/mL (∼1 mg/mL) stock) per 1 g of wet cells to the bacterial cell pellet. After gentle shaking for 10 min, collect the pellets by centrifugation at 14,500xg for 20 min, and then suspend in 15 mL of B-per Reagent diluted 10 fold. After gentle shaking for 10 min, collect the inclusion body pellets by centrifugation at 14,500xg for 20 min.

steps.title: Transform plasmid for 197 bp DNA
steps.instruction: Transform 1 µL of pUC19‑197x16_W601 (≈100 ng/µL) into 50 µL NEB Stable cells, spread ~20 µL cells on LB agar with 100 µg/mL ampicillin, incubate 37 °C for ~18 h.

steps.title: Inoculate colonies and isolate plasmid
steps.instruction: Label 4 colonies, inoculate each into 10 mL LB +100 µg/mL ampicillin in 50 mL Falcon tubes, grow 37 °C, 220 rpm for 6–8 h; transfer 4 mL from each tube to new tubes and extract plasmid with Promega Mini‑Prep Kit.

steps.title: Verify plasmids by restriction digest
steps.instruction: Digest 200 ng of each purified plasmid with PstI + EcoRI (expect 3.2 kb insert, 2.7 kb vector) or with SmaI alone (expect 197 bp insert, 2.9 kb vector) and resolve on 2 % agarose gel.

steps.title: Scale‑up culture and harvest plasmid
steps.instruction: Combine verified cultures, distribute equally into six 1 L flasks containing 2×YT medium, incubate 37 °C, 250 rpm for 18–24 h; harvest cells at 4000 × g, 4 °C, 30 min, then perform large‑scale plasmid prep (Dyer et al., 2004).

steps.title: Digest plasmid to release 197 bp DNA
steps.instruction: Adjust plasmid to ~2 mg/mL in DI water, add 10 U SmaI per mg plasmid in 1× Cutsmart buffer, incubate 37 °C for 18 h; if incomplete (extra bands on 2 % gel), add 50 % more enzyme and incubate another 18 h.

steps.title: Precipitate plasmid backbone
steps.instruction: Aliquot digestion to ~20 mL portions, add 40 % PEG 6000 stepwise to reach 4–6 % final PEG while adding 4 M NaCl to 0.5 M final; mix, place on ice ≥1 h, centrifuge 4000 × g, 4 °C, 30 min, discard ~15 mL supernatant per tube.

steps.title: Precipitate 197 bp DNA
steps.instruction: To the remaining supernatant add ~30 mL cold ethanol, centrifuge 4000 × g, 4 °C, 30 min, discard supernatant, wash pellet three times with 70 % ethanol, air‑dry, resuspend in TE 10/1 (10 mM Tris, 1 mM EDTA, pH 8.0).

steps.title: Phenol‑chloroform cleanup and final storage
steps.instruction: Extract DNA once with PCIA (25:24:1) then with CIA, precipitate with ethanol, redissolve in TE 10/1; typical yield 30–40 mg, store at 4 °C (~5 mg/mL).

steps.title: Clone H1 and ProTα into expression vectors
steps.instruction: Insert codon‑optimized H1 and ProTα genes into pET42b or pET28b using NdeI and BamHI; add C‑terminal His₆ tag for Ni‑NTA purification.

steps.title: Lyse cells and bind to Ni‑NTA
steps.instruction: Resuspend cell pellet in 50 mL lysis buffer (50 mM Na‑phosphate, 8 M urea or 4 M guanidine, 0.75 M NaCl, 5 mM imidazole, pH 8.0); sonicate 15 s ON/1 min OFF, 15 % power, total 4 min; centrifuge 130 000 × g, 20 °C, 1 h; mix supernatant with 2 mL Ni‑NTA beads in Econo column, rock 1 h.

steps.title: Wash and elute His‑tagged protein
steps.instruction: Wash beads stepwise with 10 mL wash buffer (50 mM Na‑phosphate, 6 M urea, 0.5 M NaCl, pH 8.0) containing 5, 10, 15, 20, 25 mM imidazole; elute with 5 × 8 mL elution buffer (50 mM Na‑phosphate, pH 8.0, 6 M urea, 0.5 M NaCl, 250 mM imidazole), analyze fractions by SDS‑PAGE.

steps.title: RP‑HPLC purification and lyophilization
steps.instruction: Pool protein‑containing fractions, inject onto reverse‑phase HPLC column, elute with linear acetonitrile gradient 10 %→60 %; freeze peak on dry ice and lyophilize; store lyophilized powder at 22 °C (dark) or –80 °C.

steps.title: Transform scFv plasmid into BL21(DE3) RIPL
steps.instruction: Transform 1 µL pETHis6TEV‑scFv into 20 µL BL21(DE3) RIPL, spread ~20 µL on LB agar +100 µg/mL ampicillin, incubate 37 °C 18 h.

steps.title: Grow starter culture
steps.instruction: Inoculate a single colony into 10 mL LB +100 µg/mL ampicillin, grow 37 °C, 220 rpm, 14 h.

steps.title: Scale up expression and induce
steps.instruction: Dilute starter into 1 L 2×YT +100 µg/mL ampicillin, grow to OD₆₀₀ ≈ 0.8; cool shaker to 25 °C, add 0.5 mM IPTG, continue 25 °C, 220 rpm, 16 h.

steps.title: Harvest cells and lyse
steps.instruction: Centrifuge 3000 × g, 10 min, 4 °C; resuspend pellet in 35 mL lysis buffer (50 mM Tris‑HCl pH 7.5, 100 mM NaCl, 1 mM EDTA), add 0.5 mL 50 mg/mL lysozyme, freeze on dry ice.

steps.title: Thaw and sonicate inclusion bodies
steps.instruction: Thaw at 42 °C water bath, sonicate 15 s ON/1 min OFF, 15 % power, total 4 min on ice; pellet inclusion bodies at 27 000 × g, 20 min, 4 °C.

steps.title: Wash inclusion bodies
steps.instruction: Resuspend pellet in wash buffer (50 mM Tris‑HCl pH 7.5, 100 mM NaCl, 1 mM EDTA, 1 % Triton X‑100); if sticky, sonicate 30 s; centrifuge, discard supernatant; repeat wash twice more with lysis buffer.

steps.title: Refolding solution cleanup
steps.instruction: Collect all refolding solution in a 2 L beaker, adjust pH to ~7.8 with ~2.6 mL 35 % HCl at 4 °C, centrifuge 4000 × g, 4 °C, 10 min, filter supernatant through 0.22 µm filter.

steps.title: Bind scFv to SP Sepharose
steps.instruction: Equilibrate 4 mL SP Sepharose Fast Flow with 20 mL SP binding buffer (20 mM Tris‑HCl pH 7.4), then 20 mL with 1 M NaCl, then 20 mL buffer again; add resin to refolding solution, stir 150 rpm, bind 1 h at 4 °C.

steps.title: SP chromatography and elution
steps.instruction: Pass solution through Econo column, collect flow‑through; wash resin with total 150 mL SP binding buffer (10 mL ×15), then twice with buffer containing 100 mM NaCl; elute with 48 mL SP elution buffer (20 mM Tris‑HCl pH 7.4, 300 mM NaCl) in six 8 mL fractions; measure OD₂₈₀ (second fraction ≈0.3–0.6).

steps.title: Analyze SP fractions and pool
steps.instruction: Run SP fractions and flow‑through on SDS‑PAGE; discard flow‑through if no scFv; pooled scFv yield ≈10–15 mg.

steps.title: HisTrap polishing chromatography
steps.instruction: Equilibrate 5 mL HisTrap column with 5 CV wash buffer (20 mM Tris‑HCl pH 7.4, 40 mM imidazole, 300 mM NaCl), 5 CV elution buffer (20 mM Tris‑HCl pH 7.4, 500 mM imidazole, 300 mM NaCl), then wash buffer again; add 1/10 v/v elution buffer to pooled SP fractions (final imidazole ≈44 mM), load onto column, wash 5 CV, elute with linear gradient 40 → 250 mM imidazole over 20 CV using AKTA FPLC; collect main peak (~80 mL), SDS‑PAGE confirm, yield ≈5–10 mg, concentrate to ~4 mL.

steps.title: Size‑exclusion chromatography of scFv
steps.instruction: Equilibrate Superdex S75 10/600 with Gel‑Filtration buffer A (20 mM Tris‑HCl pH 7.4, 150 mM NaCl, 1 mM EDTA) for 2 CV; inject 2 mL scFv at 1 mL/min, collect fractions; scFv elutes ~65 mL, verify by SDS‑PAGE.

steps.title: Concentrate and store scFv
steps.instruction: Concentrate peak fractions to ~1.5 mL using 10 kDa Amicon device, keep concentration ≈5 µM (avoid >5 mg/mL); final yield ≈3–5 mg, store at 4 °C.

steps.title: Prepare H1 and ProTα for chromatosome
steps.instruction: Dissolve ~5 mg each of H1 and ProTα powder in 0.5 mL nuclease‑free water, rock 30 min; mix with 0.5 mL gel‑filtration buffer B (20 mM Tris‑HCl pH 7.4, 1 mM EDTA, 600 mM NaCl).

steps.title: Remove aggregates and gel‑filter H1/ProTα
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 27 000 × g, 4 °C, 15 min; inject supernatant onto Superdex S75 10/300GL pre‑equilibrated in buffer B, run 0.75 mL/min on AKTA, collect peak fractions and determine concentrations.

steps.title: Prepare native PAGE gel
steps.instruction: Cast 4.8 % native PAGE gel, pre‑run in 0.2× TBE at 120 V, 4 °C for 2 h.

steps.title: Titrate nucleosome with H1
steps.instruction: Dilute nucleosome, ProTα, and H1 in TEN10 buffer (10 mM Tris‑HCl pH 7.4, 1 mM EDTA, 10 mM NaCl, 0.5 mM TCEP) to 1 µM, 2 µM, and 1 µM respectively; set up 10 µL reactions containing 100 nM nucleosome, 200 nM ProTα, 2 % Ficoll 400, and H1 at 50, 75, 100, 125, 150, 175, or 200 nM; incubate 25 °C 15 min.

steps.title: Run native PAGE of titrations
steps.instruction: Load 5 µL of each reaction onto the pre‑run gel, run in 0.2× TBE at 100 V for 120 min at 4 °C; stain with Midori Green Advance, image with ChemiDoc.

steps.title: Determine optimal nucleosome:H1 ratio
steps.instruction: Analyze gel to select the H1 concentration giving the desired chromatosome band; avoid nucleosome/H1 concentrations >100 µM to prevent aggregation; for scale‑up, keep both components <10 µM and prepare >100 µL chromatosome by titrating nucleosome with H1 in presence of ProTα.

steps.title: Add scFv to chromatosome
steps.instruction: Dilute scFv in TEN10 to ~0.5 µM, add 3‑fold molar excess scFv to the chromatosome sample, incubate on ice 15 min.

steps.title: Polish scFv‑chromatosome complex
steps.instruction: Concentrate mixture to ~500 µL, inject onto Superose 6 10/300GL pre‑equilibrated with TEN10, run at 0.5 mL/min on AKTA, collect peak fraction, concentrate to ~100 µL using 30 kDa MWCO Amicon filter; store complex for cryo‑EM grid preparation.
